title: Sessionized latency vs cost — quick cheat sheet
content:
Purpose:
A short, practical reference for product/solutions folks and SREs evaluating sessionized (long-lived) sessions vs short-lived cold requests.

Scope & quick summary:
- Workloads: chat-style 1:many-turn sessions and single-turn generation.
- Models profiled: Llama2-13B (q8_0), Llama2-70B (q4_0), trimmed distill-ish 7B variant (q4_0).
- Hardware: H100-80GB for heavy, A100-40GB for mid, and small Ampere nodes for 7B.
- Primary metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) for a single generation op (512 tokens context, 64 tokens output) and effective cost per 1k output tokens (in USD equivalent using internal unit cost).

Experiment notes (how to interpret):
- "Sessionized" means persistent KV cache reused across turns; warmup cost amortized across subsequent turns.
- "Cold" means no KV cache reuse; includes model load or cold JIT penalty for the caller's typical latency window.
- Batches: we compare 1x (no batching) and opportunistic 4x coalesced batching.
- Output token cost uses our platform token accounting + GPU-minute amortization over a measured throughput window. Not absolute cloud $s, but comparable across runs.

ASCII summary table (512 ctx, 64 out):

Platform slice | Model (quant) | Mode | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | cost/1k out (USD equiv)
---------------|---------------|------|---------|---------|---------|---------------------
H100-80 | 70B (q4) | cold | 310 | 540 | 920 | 8.5
H100-80 | 70B (q4) | sessionized (turn 5+) | 95 | 180 | 300 | 2.1
A100-40 | 70B (q4) | cold | 420 | 760 | 1250 | 11.2
A100-40 | 70B (q4) | sessionized (turn 5+) | 130 | 260 | 440 | 2.9
A100-40 | 13B (q8) | cold | 120 | 210 | 380 | 3.1
A100-40 | 13B (q8) | sessionized (turn 3+) | 45 | 90 | 160 | 0.9
Small Ampere | 7B (q4) | cold | 45 | 95 | 210 | 0.7
Small Ampere | 7B (q4) | sessionized (turn 2+) | 25 | 50 | 85 | 0.3

Key observations from the table:
- Sessionization reduces observed p50 latency by ~60–75% for large models once warm. p95/p99 improvements are larger because KV reuse avoids repeated attention computation on cached prefix.
- Cost per 1k tokens drops dramatically with sessionization: best-case 4–6x improvement on 70B when sessions last multiple turns. For smaller models the delta is smaller but still material.
- Cold penalties on A100 are higher than H100 for 70B on these builds (likely kernel selection + memory pressure differences).

Turn-level amortization sketch (example):
- Scenario: customer chat average 6 turns, average 32 input tokens / 64 output tokens.
- 70B cold per-turn GPU time ~0.9s; with sessionization first-turn 0.9s, subsequent turns ~0.28s. Weighted avg over 6 turns -> effective per-turn GPU time ~0.4s. Cost scaling ~= 2.25x cheaper vs naive cold-only billing.

Batching interplay notes:
- Opportunistic batching (4x) improved throughput and lowered cost/1k by an extra ~15–30% for cold bursts, but it increased p95 by ~10–25% for single-request latency-sensitive flows.
- Sessionized workloads are less dependent on batching for cost gains (because KV reuse already reduces compute); mixing both gives best cost but watch tail latency bounds.

Text charts (tokenized cost vs session length) — rough numbers (normalized to cold=1.0):
- 70B q4 on H100: session length 1 -> cost 1.0; len 2 -> 0.48; len 4 -> 0.27; len 8 -> 0.16; len 16 -> 0.11.
- 13B q8 on A100: session length 1 -> 1.0; len 2 -> 0.62; len 4 -> 0.38; len 8 -> 0.25.

Operational recommendations (practical):
- If workload median session length >= 3 turns: strongly prefer sessionized APIs (pin session IDs + KV cache hints). Big wins for 13B+ model families.
- For strict p99 SLOs on single-turn UIs: avoid opportunistic batching on the critical path; consider a dual-path: low-latency route (no batching, smaller model) + cost-optimized route (batching, larger model) with routing fallback.
- Use adaptive quantization profiles: 70B q4 for throughput-critical background generation; 13B q8 for interactive UI where p50 < 150ms is needed.
- Tune autoscaler to maintain a warm pool sized for median concurrency, not peak. Warm pool avoids cold starts that dominate first-turn cost.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate these numbers on private deployments with customer-specific NVLink topologies (we saw A100 variance across instances).
- Re-run with streaming output overhead accounted (above numbers assume full-token generation measured at end).
- Add per-GB network egress cost overlay for cross-region routing decisions (affects hosted multi-region fallbacks).

Quick stuff for sales/solutions (one-liner bullets):
- "If your app averages >3 chat turns, expect 2–5x lower token costs by enabling sessionized inference and modest warm pools."
- "For sub-150ms interactive p50, prefer 13B q8 on A100 with sessionized routing; for background high-volume generation, favor 70B q4 on H100 with batching and longer sessions."

Notes to self / provenance:
- Runs from Feb 2–12 2026 on staging cluster r-runtime-perf-02. Kernel stack: TRT-optimized runtime v1.8. Patch set includes kvcache-async prefetch from PR 942.
- Rough numbers: see linked artifacts for raw CSVs (WIP).

Contact: ava@redwood.ai if you want the raw traces or a quick runbook to reproduce.

End of cheat sheet.
